name: uk.co.fileclerk/filing-tools
title: FileClerk
description: UK company filing deadlines, filed figures and iXBRL validation

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Find a UK company's number from its name on the Companies House register: up to 20 matches, each with company_number, company_name, company_status and locality (the town of the registered office), active companies first, and url (the company's page on FileClerk). For a name with no number: company_number is the input of get_company_deadlines, get_company_finances and run_company_tools. name is 2 to 160 characters; a part of the name is enough. Searches have their own limit of 600 per hour.

name.description: All or a part of the company's name, 2 to 160 characters.

tools.name: get_company_deadlines
tools.description: Is a UK company in good standing on the Companies House register, and what must happen next? Returns a verdict (act_now, coming_up, all_clear), `nearest` (the nearest open date of all) and one entry per obligation (annual accounts, confirmation statement, each director's and PSC's identity verification, CT600 return and Corporation Tax payment as estimates, payroll when inferred), each with status, due date, basis (register, estimate or inferred), what can happen if missed and its official source, and `time_limits`, the last day of each open claim or change (amendment, R&D notification, loss and overpayment relief) with what it is for and its source. 6 to 9 KB for most companies. `detail: "full"` adds each card's details, risks and official links, the timeline, the track record and register changes, at about 3 to 4 times the size. Dates are calendar dates in `timezone`; day counts are for `as_of`. `url` is the company's page on FileClerk. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

company_number.description: A Companies House company number, such as 00445790 or SC123456.

detail.description: How much to return. Left out: summary. full adds each card's details, risks and official links, the timeline, the track record and register changes.

tools.name: get_company_finances
tools.description: Filed figures for a UK company from its last 10 annual accounts on the Companies House register, as tagged in the filed iXBRL: net assets, cash, working capital, average employees, the balance sheet lines, and turnover and profit when the company files them (small and micro companies may leave them out, so they are often null). Also who signed the accounts, when, the accounting standard, audit status, the route they were filed by (filed_via; web_service says WebFiling or Companies House online), and `software`, the software they were made with as named in the filing's hidden tag "Name of production software", when FileClerk knows the name. A year filed as PDF only takes the prior-year column of the next year's iXBRL accounts (source: comparative); else, when FileClerk has read its scanned pages, a figure is kept only when the totals or the OCR digits confirm it (source: pdf-read); scannable is true for a scanned year that FileClerk has not read, reading while a read is queued. `url` is the company's finances page on FileClerk. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

company_number.description: A Companies House company number, such as 00445790 or SC123456.

tools.name: get_scan_progress
tools.description: How far FileClerk has got in reading a UK company's accounts filed as scanned PDFs. items has one entry per scanned filing still waiting or being read: made_up_to; ahead (reads in the queue before it; 0 while it is read); started_at (epoch ms; null while it waits); and stage, null while it waits, else one of download (downloading the PDF from the register), render (preparing the pages), ocr (finding the statements, page done of total), claude (reading the balance sheet and profit and loss; total is the pages read, done stays 0) and check (checking the totals). done and total count pages in ocr and claude only; in download, render and check both are 0. items is empty when no read is waiting or under way. now is the server time in epoch ms. It counts against no limit.

company_number.description: A Companies House company number, such as 00445790 or SC123456.

tools.name: get_accounts_route_counts
tools.description: How the active companies people looked up on FileClerk filed their last annual accounts at Companies House, counted by the year those accounts were made up to. Each company counts once, as FileClerk last read it. software: iXBRL that no Companies House service made; webfiling: iXBRL from Companies House WebFiling; companies_house_online: iXBRL from another Companies House online service; paper: the register marks the filing as paper; unknown: FileClerk could not tell, as no iXBRL was read and the register does not mark it as paper. The companies are those FileClerk's sitemap lists: a person asked about each one by a search on the site, a follow, a saved company, a calendar feed, a call with an API key or over MCP, or their own assistant. So the counts cover those companies, not the whole register. From 1 April 2028 Companies House takes accounts only from software; WebFiling and paper stop taking them. counted_at is when FileClerk counted; a count is kept for up to an hour. It names no software. It reads only FileClerk's own copies and counts against no limit. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

tools.name: follow_companies
tools.description: Start FileClerk deadline email alerts for up to 50 UK companies at once. FileClerk emails one confirmation link to the address; nothing is sent until the person clicks it. Returns each input as followed, not_found, invalid or duplicate. It is for the person's own email address, with their consent.

email.description: The person's own email address. FileClerk sends one confirmation link to it.

company_numbers.description: Up to 50 Companies House company numbers, such as 00445790.

tools.name: find_companies
tools.description: Find UK companies on the Companies House register by filters, without a name: sic (5-digit SIC code), type (ltd, plc, llp, community-interest-company, private-limited-guarant-nsc, limited-partnership, charitable-incorporated-organisation ...), status (active, dissolved, liquidation ...), location (registered office address), from and to (incorporation dates, YYYY-MM-DD). location takes words of the registered office address, such as a town or a postcode (LS1 or LS1 5EN). Every word must be in the address, so a county finds only the addresses that include it. 50 per page, each with url (the company's page on FileClerk); hits counts every match, pages reach the first 10,000. There is no filter on accounts type (such as dormant or micro-entity) or on whether a company is part of a group: Companies House's search has neither. sic 99999 finds companies that give Dormant Company as their nature of business.

type.description: Company type as Companies House names it, such as ltd, plc, llp or community-interest-company.

status.description: Company status, such as active, dissolved or liquidation.

location.description: Words of the registered office address, such as a town or a postcode (LS1 or LS1 5EN). Every word must be in the address, so a county finds only the addresses that include it.

page.description: Page of results, from 1. A page has 50 companies.

tools.name: export_companies
tools.description: The link to a CSV file of the UK companies on the Companies House register that match filters, without a name: sic, type, status, location, from and to, as in a filtered search. Answers hits (every match), rows (the companies the file holds, at most 5,000) and csv_url (the file on FileClerk, one row per company: number, name, status, type, incorporation date, locality, postcode and SIC codes). The answer holds no companies. When hits is over 5,000, the file holds 5,000 of them, in no date order. There is no page: export again with narrower incorporation dates (from and to) that do not overlap, until each answer's hits is 5,000 or less, and use those files instead of this one. Each opening of csv_url is one export for whoever opens it: 2 an hour with no FileClerk account, 50 a day with one.

type.description: Company type as Companies House names it, such as ltd, plc, llp or community-interest-company.

status.description: Company status, such as active, dissolved or liquidation.

location.description: Words of the registered office address, such as a town or a postcode (LS1 or LS1 5EN). Every word must be in the address, so a county finds only the addresses that include it.

tools.name: search_officers
tools.description: Find UK company officers (directors, secretaries, LLP members) by name on the Companies House register: up to 20 matches with officer_id, name and number of appointments. No birth date, nationality or address. get_officer takes an officer_id and gives that officer's companies.

q.description: All or a part of the officer's name, 3 to 160 characters.

tools.name: get_officer
tools.description: Every appointment of one Companies House officer by officer_id (from search_officers): company number and name, role, appointed and resigned dates, company status, current first, with FileClerk's verdict (act_now, coming_up, all_clear) for companies in its cache. Counts as one lookup.

officer_id.description: The officer_id of one officer, as search_officers returns it.

tools.name: validate_accounts
tools.description: Check UK company iXBRL accounts (micro-entity, dormant or small, FRS 102 / FRS 105) before filing with Companies House. Pass the whole XHTML file as text (up to 10 MB). Returns one finding per check, the Companies House accounts rules and the company's register record (number, name, status, period end), each reject, risk, not_evaluated or pass with its rule. reject means Companies House rejects it (the V checks are confirmed on its test validator; the R checks find the company missing, closed or under another name); risk means the TIS requires it but rejection is not confirmed. The file is never stored. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

ixbrl.description: The whole iXBRL accounts file (XHTML) as text, up to 10 MB.

tools.name: prepare_accounts
tools.description: Prepare a dry run for annual accounts. Read registered identity and period defaults, calculate totals and return the checked iXBRL and validation findings. When the current period has no income and only small costs, it also suggests checking whether dormant accounts fit. When the accounts are ready, it also lists figure checks: a figure ten times or more, or a tenth or less, of the same figure in the comparative period, as advice that never blocks. No submission or payment occurs.

draft.description: The accounts to prepare: company number, trading state, the figures of the current period (and of the prior period, if there is one), the notes, the approval date and the signatory.

eligibility.description: The size and audit answers for these accounts: audit_exemption_confirmed and, where they apply, group, excluded, prior_dormant and last_size.

tools.name: prepare_cic_package
tools.description: Prepare a community interest company's accounts package for Companies House: the director-approved accounts (iXBRL, up to 10 MB) and a simplified CIC34 report built from the answers, in one ZIP with the folders the Accounts TIS sets. The register gives the company name and the open accounts period. Returns ready, findings (the accounts checks V01–V10 and the package checks P01–P05, each with its rule), and once ready the ZIP as base64 in zip.data and human_step: a person uploads the ZIP at Companies House and pays the £15 fee there. Nothing is filed or stored. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

company_number.description: The Companies House company number, such as 00445790 or SC123456. Leading zeros may be left out.

accounts_ixbrl.description: The director-approved accounts for the open period, as the whole iXBRL (XHTML) file text, up to 10 MB.

report.description: simplified: the short CIC34 report, which most community interest companies file. A company that paid performance-related interest on a debt or debenture, or a company limited by shares that declared or proposed to declare dividends in respect of the financial year to which the report relates or has declared a dividend in respect of any of the four financial years immediately preceding that financial year, files the detailed report, which is not prepared here.

activities.description: Part 1: the company's activities in the financial year and how they benefited the community, up to 12,000 characters.

consultation.description: Part 2: confirmed_none when no stakeholder consultation was held; disclosed with the stakeholders, how they were consulted and the action taken in response, each up to 12,000 characters.

directors_remuneration.description: Part 3: confirmed_none when the directors received no remuneration; disclosed with total, the overall total in whole pounds of the directors' pay, long-term incentive payments and company pension contributions (Community Interest Company Regulations 2005, Schedule 4A, paragraph 1(1)).

asset_transfers.description: Part 4: confirmed_none when no asset was transferred other than for full consideration; disclosed with the details of each transfer, including the amount or a fair estimate of the value.

signatory.description: Part 5: the name of the director who signed the report.

signed_on.description: The day the director signed the report, YYYY-MM-DD; on or after the period end and not after today.

approved_and_signed.description: true: the directors approved these accounts and the signatory, a director, signed this report.

cic34.description: The CIC34 answers: the report type, Parts 1 to 4, the director who signed (Part 5) and the directors' confirmation.

tools.name: prepare_ct600
tools.description: Calculate a Company Tax Return (CT600) as a dry run. Pass one set of whole-pound figures for each Corporation Tax accounting period of the accounts. Returns each period's CT600 boxes with HMRC box numbers, the tax and the findings to settle. With an identity (company name, number, UTR, optional accounts iXBRL), also builds each return's HMRC XML and checks it against the CT600 schemas and HMRC's local validation rules. Nothing is sent to HMRC or stored.

period_start_on.description: First day of the company's accounting period for Corporation Tax, YYYY-MM-DD.

period_end_on.description: Last day of the accounting period, YYYY-MM-DD; at most 12 months after the start.

opening_balance.description: Whole pounds owed from loans made before this period (already charged in their own period). Repayments clear it first.

loans.description: Loans made in the period. Each has on (the date, YYYY-MM-DD), amount (whole pounds) and, for the CT600A, participator (the borrower's name).

repayments.description: Repayments, releases and write-offs in or after the period. Each has on (the date, YYYY-MM-DD), amount (whole pounds) and released (true for a release or a write-off). They clear the oldest loan first.

return.description: The return's figures: kind (trading, property, mixed or dormant), the first and last day of the accounts, and one set of whole-pound figures for each Corporation Tax accounting period.

identity.description: Company name, company number, the 10-digit UTR and, to check the company number in them, the accounts as iXBRL. With an identity, each return's HMRC XML is built and checked. It is not stored.

tools.name: calculate_deadlines
tools.description: Work out a UK company's first deadlines from its incorporation date, without a company number: first accounts due date (with the Companies Act 2006 s442 rule used), first confirmation statement, and CT600 and Corporation Tax payment dates (estimates; a first period over 12 months gets two CT periods; none for an LLP). kind is ltd, llp or plc. Give period_end_on only when the first period does not end on the default date (last day of the anniversary month), and shortened_on when an AA01 shortened it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

kind.description: Company type: ltd, llp or plc.

period_end_on.description: End of the first accounts period, YYYY-MM-DD. Left out: the last day of the anniversary month (Companies Act 2006 s391(4)).

shortened_on.description: Date an AA01 that shortened the first period was filed, YYYY-MM-DD (s442(4)).

tools.name: calculate_penalty
tools.description: Work out UK late filing penalties and interest for given dates: the Companies House accounts penalty (private or public bands, doubled when last year's accounts were also late), CT600 flat penalties by the return's filing date (higher for returns due on or after 1 April 2026; third late in a row is higher), the tax-geared penalty (10% or 20% of unpaid tax) and HMRC late payment interest day by day across rate changes. Money is integer pence. A missing filed or paid date is measured to today. Interest assumes a 365-day year. Nothing is stored.

kind.description: Company type: ltd, llp or plc. A plc has the public company penalty bands.

today.description: The day a penalty is measured to when a filed or paid date is missing, YYYY-MM-DD. Left out: today.

accounts.description: The annual accounts: due_on, filed_on when they are filed, and late_last_year (true when last year's accounts were also late). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

ct.description: The Corporation Tax period: period_end_on and, when known, return_due_on, filed_on, third_late, unpaid_pence, payment_due_on and paid_on. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD and money is integer pence.

tools.name: calculate_corporation_tax
tools.description: Work out UK Corporation Tax for a period of accounts (from 1 April 2015, up to 18 months): taxable total profits in whole pounds, the period dates (YYYY-MM-DD) and the number of associated companies. Splits a period over 12 months into two accounting periods and each at 31 March, applies 19%/25% with marginal relief (3/200) from 1 April 2023, reduces the limits for a short period and divides them among associated companies. Returns integer pence per part and per period, with the payment date. Nothing is stored.

period_start_on.description: First day of the period that the accounts cover, YYYY-MM-DD.

period_end_on.description: Last day of the period, YYYY-MM-DD; at most 18 months after the start.

profits.description: Taxable total profits for the whole period, after reliefs, in whole pounds.

associated.description: Number of associated companies in the period (control, CTA 2010 s18E), not counting this one.

tools.name: calculate_s455
tools.description: Work out UK s455 tax on a director's (participator's) loan from a close company for one accounting period (at most 12 months): loans made in the period with dates and whole-pound amounts, repayments with dates, and the balance owed from earlier periods. Each loan at the rate for its date (35.75% from 6 April 2026); repayments clear the oldest debt first; nothing to pay on what is repaid before the due date (9 months and 1 day after the period end); later repayments are reclaims with their earliest date. Warns on the 30-day rule. Integer pence out. Nothing is stored.

period_start_on.description: First day of the company's accounting period for Corporation Tax, YYYY-MM-DD.

period_end_on.description: Last day of the accounting period, YYYY-MM-DD; at most 12 months after the start.

opening_balance.description: Whole pounds owed from loans made before this period (already charged in their own period). Repayments clear it first.

loans.description: Loans made in the period. Each has on (the date, YYYY-MM-DD), amount (whole pounds) and, for the CT600A, participator (the borrower's name).

repayments.description: Repayments, releases and write-offs in or after the period. Each has on (the date, YYYY-MM-DD), amount (whole pounds) and released (true for a release or a write-off). They clear the oldest loan first.

tools.name: calculate_income_tax
tools.description: Work out UK take-home pay from gross pay: income tax by band (England, Wales, Northern Ireland, or Scotland's bands from 2017-18), employee Class 1 National Insurance with mid-year rate changes, student loans (plan1, plan2, plan4, plan5, postgraduate) and net pay per year, month and week, for tax years 2011-12 to 2026-27 (tax_year like "2026-27"). gross_pence is pay for one frequency period (year, month, week, day, hour). Standard tax code, no pension. Integer pence out. Nothing is stored. The result is general information from the published rules, not professional tax advice.

gross_pence.description: Gross pay in pence for one frequency period.

frequency.description: The period that gross_pence covers: year, month, week, day or hour.

hours_per_week.description: Hours worked a week, for hourly pay: over 0 and at most 100. 37.5 when left out.

days_per_week.description: Days worked a week, for daily pay: over 0 and at most 7. 5 when left out.

tax_year.description: Tax year from 2011-12 to 2026-27, such as 2026-27 (6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027).

region.description: Where the person pays income tax: england, wales, northern_ireland or scotland. Scotland has its own bands from 2017-18.

plan.description: Student loan plan: plan1, plan2, plan4 or plan5. Left out: no student loan.

postgraduate.description: true when the person also repays a postgraduate loan.

tools.name: calculate_director_pay
tools.description: Work out a UK company director's salary and dividends for one tax year from 2016-17 (tax_year like "2026-27"): income tax, dividend tax and employee NI for the director; employer NI, Corporation Tax on the profit left and retained profit for the company; and the total tax. profit_pence is the company's profit before the director's salary and employer NI. other_employees: true allows the Employment Allowance. Integer pence in and out. Nothing is stored. The result is general information from the published rules, not professional tax advice.

tax_year.description: Tax year, such as 2026-27. From 2016-17, the first year of the dividend allowance.

region.description: Where the director pays income tax: england, wales, northern_ireland or scotland.

salary_pence.description: The director's salary for the tax year, in pence.

dividends_pence.description: Dividends paid to the director in the tax year, in pence.

profit_pence.description: The company's profit for the year before the director's salary and employer NI, in pence.

other_employees.description: true when someone else is on the payroll above the secondary threshold, so the Employment Allowance can apply.

associated.description: Number of companies that the company is associated with (control), for the Corporation Tax limits.

tools.name: check_company_size
tools.description: Is a UK company micro, small, medium or large for its accounts? Uses the limits for financial years beginning on or after 6 April 2025 (two of three: turnover, balance sheet total, average monthly staff), the two-year rule (give last_year, or first_year: true; and last_size when one year meets a limit and the other misses it), and pro-rates turnover by months. Returns the size, what it may file, and whether it is exempt from audit, each with its Companies Act section. Money in whole pounds. Nothing is stored.

this_year.description: This financial year's figures: turnover and balance_sheet in whole pounds, employees (the monthly average) and months (the length of the year; 12 when left out).

last_year.description: The same figures for the financial year before. Left out only for the first financial year.

first_year.description: true when this is the company's first financial year.

last_size.description: The size the company qualified as last year: micro, small, medium or large. It decides the answer when one year meets a limit and the other does not.

excluded.description: true for a public company, bank, insurer, e-money issuer, MiFID or UCITS firm, insurance market or Master Trust funder (Companies Act 2006 s384).

group.description: true when the company is a parent or a subsidiary in a group: the group tests apply (s383, s479).

tools.name: check_strike_off
tools.description: Can a UK company apply to be struck off the register (DS01) now? Reads the Companies House register (status, filings in the last 3 months, a strike-off already applied for, outstanding charges) and takes three answers: traded or sold stock, an open insolvency or court case, other activity, each in the last 3 months (true means yes; leave out to get verdict answer_questions). Returns can_apply, not_yet with each bar and its Companies Act section, or closed, plus warnings and the steps (fee, 7-day copy duty). Counts as one lookup.

company_number.description: A Companies House company number, such as 00445790 or SC123456.

answers.description: Three answers, where true means yes. traded: the company traded or sold stock in the last 3 months. insolvency: an insolvency process, arrangement or court application is open. activity: the company did something else in the last 3 months beyond closing down. Left out: the verdict is answer_questions.

tools.name: check_2028_filing
tools.description: From 1 April 2028 UK company accounts must be filed by software as iXBRL. For 1 to 50 company numbers, returns how each company's latest annual accounts were filed (paper, pdf, webfiling or software; webfiling: Companies House WebFiling or another Companies House online service, and web_service says which, webfiling or companies_house_online; both close for accounts on 1 April 2028) and must_move or ready, with no_accounts, not_found, invalid, unknown or limit otherwise. Each number counts as one lookup on the hourly limit.

company_numbers.description: 1 to 50 Companies House company numbers, such as 00445790.

tools.name: run_company_tools
tools.description: Every FileClerk tool on one UK company at once: how its last accounts were filed and whether it must move to software by 1 April 2028; whether it can apply to be struck off (pass traded, insolvency and activity as true or false; leave out for verdict answer_questions); its size from the two newest filed accounts (null when they carry too few figures); and the accounts late filing penalty if filed today (null without a due date). `url` is the company's tools page on FileClerk. Counts as one lookup.

company_number.description: A Companies House company number, such as 00445790 or SC123456.

traded.description: Strike-off answer: true when the company traded or sold stock in the last 3 months.

insolvency.description: Strike-off answer: true when an insolvency process, arrangement or court application is open.

activity.description: Strike-off answer: true when the company did something else in the last 3 months beyond closing down.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Send the person's error report, feedback or question to the people who run FileClerk. Answers status sent: FileClerk has received it; it is emailed to them, up to 50 a day from everyone. 5 messages an hour from one internet connection (IP address), counted together with the contact form on the site.

kind.description: error (something in FileClerk is wrong), feedback or question.

message.description: The person's message in their own words.

email.description: The person's own email address, only when they want a reply.

quote.description: The text from FileClerk that the message is about.

company_number.description: The Companies House number of the company the message is about.

tools.name: search_help
tools.description: Search FileClerk's guides to UK company filing: deadlines and penalties, annual accounts, Corporation Tax and the CT600, HMRC error codes, trial balance exports from accounting software, and the ways to file. Any word of `query` can match: a hit that holds more of its words comes first, then one with them in its title. query is up to 200 characters; common words such as "how" and "the" are left out. Up to 12 hits, 5 when limit is left out. Each hit is a whole guide (section null, text its summary) or one of its sections (text the section in full), with checked_on, the day FileClerk last checked the guide against its official sources, and url, its page on FileClerk, the source to cite. It counts against no limit. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

query.description: Words of the question or the topic, such as "HMRC error 3001" or "late filing penalty", up to 200 characters.

limit.description: The most hits to answer, 5 when left out. A number under 1 counts as 1, and one over 12 as 12.
